description:
src/lib.rs:109-120 re-exports four upstream crates using the
`pub use foo::{self, Items...}` form, which makes the full upstream
module reachable as `pkix_chain::foo`:

    pub use pkix_aia::{self, AiaError, AiaFetcher, NoAiaFetcher};
    pub use pkix_identity::{self, IdentityError, MailboxName, ServerName};
    pub use pkix_path::{
        self, DefaultVerifier, Profile, SignatureVerifier,
        TrustAnchor, ValidatedPath, ValidationPolicy,
    };
    pub use pkix_revocation::{self, NoRevocation, RevocationChecker};

The `self` half (not just the listed items) means *every public item*
of pkix_aia / pkix_identity / pkix_path / pkix_revocation is reachable
as `pkix_chain::pkix_aia::*`, etc. README.md:204-218 documents this as
a feature (\"This crate re-exports the full public API of both
component crates\").

Implications the README does not mention:

1. Any breaking change in any of the four upstream crates is also a
   breaking change in pkix-chain — even if pkix-chain doesn't use the
   changed item itself. A new variant on `pkix_path::Error` is
   non-breaking *for pkix-path* (it's non_exhaustive), but if a caller
   was matching on `pkix_chain::pkix_path::Error::SpecificVariant`,
   they receive the same exposure.

2. pkix-chain cannot swap an upstream crate for an equivalent in the
   future (e.g., a hypothetical `pkix_path_2`) while preserving the
   `pkix_chain::pkix_path` path. That's a forever-name commitment.

3. Cargo.toml:4 already acknowledges this: \"transitively breaking:
   pkix-path 0.3 ValidatedPath re-export\". The lock-step major bump
   is the maintenance cost; it's working today because the workspace
   coordinates it. Post-1.0, with external consumers, the cost is
   borne by every downstream Cargo.lock.

Two reasonable directions:

a) Keep the `{self, ...}` form, but document the version-coupling cost
   explicitly in the crate-level rustdoc and README so callers can opt
   into the model with eyes open. Add a sentence like: \"This is a
   deliberate version-coupling commitment: pkix-chain's major version
   is bumped in lockstep with any of its upstream crates' major
   versions.\"

b) Drop the `self` half of each re-export, keeping only the named
   items. Callers who want the rest add the upstream crate themselves.
   Reduces the API surface from \"everything in 4 crates\" to \"~15
   named items\". Loses the convenience but unlocks future independent
   versioning.

(a) is cheaper and aligns with what's already shipped; the issue is
the silent commitment, not the contents.

Caller impact: indirect — manifests as forced lockstep version bumps
post-1.0. Worth documenting now while the contract is still 0.x.
title: pub use pkix_*::{self, ...} locks the major version of every upstream crate
